title: Sale of a Repossessed Vehicle, Surplus and Charge-Off — Kestrel Pre-Owned Retail
content:
**Recovery & Remarketing policy — sale and charge-off, Kestrel Pre-Owned Retail Installment Sale Contract**

**Sale.** A repossessed vehicle can be sold only while the contract status is repossessed. The sale may take place no earlier than the company minimum notice period after the notice of intent to sell was mailed. The period is counted in calendar days starting the day after the notice mailing date recorded on the contract; where the contract records a state notice period longer than the company minimum, that longer period is used in the same count, and a sale on the first day after the period is permitted.

**Proceeds.** *No longer in force:* "Net proceeds are the gross proceeds less the sale expenses and are applied to principal" — this clause has been superseded by the current deficiency terms. The contract moves to deficiency when the principal balance plus the fees due balance remains above zero, and to paid in full when the net proceeds cover it. A surplus is refunded to the customer within the surplus refund days, in calendar days, of the sale together with a surplus notice.

**Settlement.** *No longer in force:* "A deficiency balance may be settled for a lump sum of at least the minimum settlement percentage of the deficiency, which pays the contract in full; a smaller offer is not within the servicing desk's authority." This clause is no longer in force and has been superseded by the current settlement terms.

**Charge-off.** A deficiency can be charged off only while the contract status is in deficiency. A deficiency may be charged off no earlier than the charge-off period after the vehicle was sold. The period is counted in calendar days starting the day after the scheduled sale date, and charge-off on the last day of the period is permitted.

### Date boundaries (hypothetical: 15-day company minimum, no longer state period; 90-day charge-off period)

| Event | Too early | First permitted day |
|---|---|---|
| Sale after the notice of intent to sell | the 15th calendar day after the mailing date | the 16th calendar day after the mailing date |
| Charge-off after the sale | the 89th calendar day after the scheduled sale date | the 90th calendar day after the scheduled sale date |

With a recorded state notice period of 20 days, the first permitted sale day is the 21st calendar day after the mailing date.

superseded_clauses: Net proceeds are gross_proceeds less sale_expenses and are applied to principal

A deficiency balance may be settled for a lump sum of at least deficiency_settlement_min_pct percent of the deficiency, which pays the contract in full; a smaller offer is not within the servicing desk's authority.
